findings.title: Pause action is never shown in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: The pause menu item requires rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) in addition to canPause. In the new list view rulerRule is intentionally undefined, so even though the Grafana Prometheus ability can set canPause to true, the Pause/Unpause item is never rendered there. Users can no longer pause or resume Grafana rules from the list view.

findings.title: Delete action is never shown in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated by `canDelete && rulerRule`. In the new list view rulerRule is undefined, so the newly added Grafana Prometheus delete ability has no effect and users with delete permission cannot delete a Grafana rule from the list's More menu. The underlying delete handler in RuleActionsButtons.V2 operates on the rule identifier and does not need the ruler rule object.

findings.title: Silence menu action does nothing in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: Clicking Silence in AlertRuleMenu sets showSilenceDrawer to true, but the drawer is only rendered when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true. In the list view `rule` is undefined while the Prometheus-based ability still makes the Silence menu item visible, so clicking Silence opens nothing and the user cannot create a silence from the list view.

findings.title: skipToken does not neutralize the Duplicate ability for non-Grafana rules
findings.body: useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities converts skipToken to undefined, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities treats an undefined rule as supported because useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading=false for no rule. Duplicate therefore becomes [AlwaysSupported, grafana AlertingRuleCreate permission]. When AlertRuleMenu renders a cloud/data-source rule, a user who has Grafana rule-create permission but not the external rule-create permission incorrectly gets the Duplicate action via the OR of ruler and Grafana abilities.

findings.title: Combined-rule abilities no longer treat federated groups as immutable
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously used isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) and marked rules in federated groups as not supported for update/delete/pause-type actions. The refactored useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated to false, so federated Mimir rule groups can now appear editable/removable in consumers using CombinedRule abilities, regressing the previous protection for federated groups.

findings.title: Grafana recording rules lose pause and export abilities
findings.body: The Prometheus-based abilities gate Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently, and ModifyExport on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). The ruler-based path used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which includes Grafana recording rules as well as alerting rules. As a result, Grafana recording rules in the ruler-free list view cannot be paused or exported even though those actions were supported for them through the ruler-based path.

findings.title: Grafana rule list items are rendered without a React key
findings.body: The filtered results map returns GrafanaRuleListItem without passing key={key}, unlike the previous GrafanaRuleLoader branch and the data-source branch in the same switch. React will reconcile these stateful list items by index, causing console warnings and risking child state such as modals/drawers in RuleActionsButtons being associated with the wrong rule if the rendered order changes.

findings.title: Grafana rule link drops the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The deleted GrafanaRuleListItem built its view href with createReturnTo() so the rule detail view received a returnTo query parameter pointing back to the current list context. The new component links directly to /alerting/grafana/${uid}/view without returnTo, so navigation back from a rule opened from the filtered/group list loses the list context that the previous link explicitly preserved.

findings.title: Menu test codifies the missing Delete item instead of covering it
findings.body: The test grants AlertingRuleDelete globally and in folder access control and defines a delete menu selector, but the More-menu test expects exactly four menu items and never asserts Delete. This hides the regression that Delete is not rendered in the ruler-free Grafana list even for users with delete permission.
